title: Secret Slave: Kidnapped and abused for 13 years. This is my story of survival.
author: Anna Ruston (pseudonym)
target_audience: Readers of true crime and survival stories
Individuals interested in accounts of resilience in the face of abuse
Those seeking awareness about domestic abuse and captivity
Supporters of anti-abuse, anti-trafficking, and social justice causes
primary_purpose: To recount the harrowing true story of the author's 13-year ordeal as a captive and victim of systemic abuse, raising awareness about the realities of domestic slavery, trauma, and the enduring strength of the human spirit.

structure_format.narrative_style: First-person, chronological, deeply personal and descriptive
structure_format.organization: Divided into chapters that follow the author’s experiences from pre-captivity, through years of abuse, to her eventual rescue and recovery process
features: Vivid, detailed recollections of daily life and experiences
Epilogue focusing on recovery and advocacy

key_concepts_lessons: Survivors can experience extreme coercion without the possibility of simply leaving; psychological captivity can be as powerful as physical restraints.
Ongoing abuse can erode a victim’s sense of self and autonomy, but survival can also foster unlikely courage and resourcefulness.
Abuse often thrives in secrecy and is maintained by manipulation, threats, and the destruction of confidence.
Post-traumatic stress, trust issues, and difficulties adjusting to normal life are common after prolonged trauma, but healing is possible.
Stories like this can raise public awareness, challenge misconceptions about abuse, and highlight the need for vigilance and support systems in society.
notable_features: First-hand account of prolonged captivity in modern times
Focus on psychological manipulation as well as physical abuse
Detailed depiction of the lasting impact of trauma
Meant to encourage discussion and activism about hidden abuse
cultural_historical_context: Published amid rising awareness of modern slavery, coercive control, and domestic abuse in the UK and globally. The book’s release contributed to ongoing conversations about how abuse can go undetected for years and underscored the importance of supporting survivors.
reception_impact: Shocked and moved readers with its graphic, honest portrayal
Used as a touchstone for discussions on domestic abuse, modern slavery, and survivor resilience
Praised for giving a voice to the silenced and for inspiring hope despite trauma
Some critics found the details difficult to read or questioned the circumstances, but most recognized its importance for public awareness
comparable_titles: A Stolen Life by Jaycee Dugard
Slave: My True Story by Mende Nazer
Room by Emma Donoghue (fictional, but with overlapping captivity themes)
